title: Sternberg memory scanning
summary: Sternberg (1966): a subject holds 1 to 6 digits in memory and decides as fast as possible whether a test digit is one of them. Reaction time grows linearly with the number of digits, at about 38 ms per digit, and equally for yes and no answers: evidence for a serial, exhaustive scan of memory. Both of the paper's procedures are here: experiment 1 (a new series every trial, then recall) and experiment 2 (a fixed positive set per part).
references: Sternberg, S. (1966). High-speed scanning in human memory. Science, 153(3736), 652-654. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.153.3736.652
Hartley, H. O., & David, H. A. (1954). Universal bounds for mean range and extreme observation. Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 25(1), 85-99.

deviations.here: two keyboard keys (J yes, F no by default)
deviations.reason: A standard rig has no lever box; a two-key manual choice keeps the binary response. Absolute latencies may shift; the slope is the measure.

deviations.here: an on-screen disc below the digit locus, green or red
deviations.reason: A standard rig has no separate lamp; it is drawn on the same display.

deviations.original: feedback and payoffs designed to encourage speed with a low error rate (scheme not given)
deviations.here: no payoffs; the instructions ask for speed with few errors and the light gives feedback on every trial
deviations.reason: The payoff scheme is not described and paying subjects is the lab's decision; an experimenter can add one.

deviations.here: 3.75 s at 60 Hz: the 3.7 s plus three frames (the frame that shows the response, and the trial boundary), measured on simulated time
deviations.reason: alhazen shows the response frame before the light, and ends and starts trials on frames of their own; three frames is 25 ms at 120 Hz.

deviations.original: variance components from an analysis of variance with subjects as random effects (notes 6-7)
deviations.here: between-subject SD of the per-subject slopes and intercepts divided by sqrt(n)
deviations.reason: A transparent estimator of the same quantities; it needs two or more subjects.

assumed.item: Font size of the digits
assumed.value: 1.5 dva (PsychoPy text height; a digit is about 0.73 of it)
assumed.reason: The paper does not describe the display at all; a size read at a glance from a chin rest

assumed.item: Colour of the digits and background
assumed.value: white digits on the rig's mid-grey background
assumed.reason: Display not described; maximal-contrast convention

assumed.item: Typeface
assumed.value: DejaVu Sans Mono
assumed.reason: Display not described; the face alhazen registers on every rig, so all rigs draw the same glyphs

assumed.item: Gap between the digits of a series
assumed.value: 0 ms (each digit replaces the last)
assumed.reason: The paper gives only 1.2 s per digit; no blank is described

assumed.item: Form and modality of the warning signal
assumed.value: a visual + at the digit locus
assumed.reason: Not stated; a visual signal needs no audio hardware

assumed.item: Warning signal duration and warning-to-digit interval
assumed.value: 500 ms; the test digit appears at its offset
assumed.reason: Not stated

assumed.item: Which response means yes
assumed.value: J = positive (in memory)
assumed.reason: Which lever (hand) was positive is not stated; counterbalance across subjects

assumed.item: Which response means no
assumed.value: F = negative
assumed.reason: See the yes key

assumed.item: Response deadline and what happens without a response
assumed.value: 5000 ms; the trial ends and its condition is served again later in the block
assumed.reason: No deadline is described; a lever was presumably always pulled

assumed.item: How long the feedback light stays on
assumed.value: 500 ms
assumed.reason: Not stated

assumed.item: Size of the feedback light
assumed.value: a 1.0 dva disc
assumed.reason: The lamp is not described

assumed.item: Place of the feedback light
assumed.value: 2.5 dva below the digit locus
assumed.reason: The lamp is not described

assumed.item: Feedback colour for correct
assumed.value: green
assumed.reason: The paper says only that the light told the subject whether the response was correct

assumed.item: Feedback colour for wrong
assumed.value: red
assumed.reason: As above

assumed.item: How the series is recalled
assumed.value: typed on the keyboard (digits, Backspace, Enter), with an on-screen prompt
assumed.reason: The paper says the trial ended with an attempt to recall the series in order; the mode is not stated

assumed.item: Recall deadline
assumed.value: 30 s; what was typed is kept, recall marked uncommitted
assumed.reason: No deadline described; a generous cap so a session cannot stall

assumed.item: Size of on-screen text other than digits
assumed.value: 0.8 dva (font size)
assumed.reason: Prompts and announcements are not described

assumed.item: Time from the end of the recall to the next series (exp. 1)
assumed.reason: Not stated

assumed.item: Practice trials per (set size, response type) cell (exp. 1)
assumed.value: 2 (24 = 12 cells x 2), shuffled
assumed.reason: 24 practice trials are stated; their split over set sizes is not

assumed.item: Test trials per (set size, response type) cell (exp. 1)
assumed.value: 12 (144 = 12 cells x 12), shuffled
assumed.reason: 144 test trials are stated; an equal 24 per set size is inferred from 'about 95 observations per point' over 8 subjects (8 x 12 = 96)

assumed.item: Rests between blocks
assumed.value: an experimenter-resumed rest after practice (exp. 1) and after each practice and test block (exp. 2)
assumed.reason: Not described; alhazen's block break

assumed.item: Order of the three parts (exp. 2)
assumed.value: random per session; a params file may list it to counterbalance
assumed.reason: The paper does not say in which order s = 1, 2, 4 were run

assumed.item: Which digits form the positive sets (exp. 2)
assumed.value: a uniform random partition of the ten digits into x (1), y (2), z (4), w (3) per session
assumed.reason: The paper says only that the composition varied from subject to subject

assumed.item: Practice test digits (exp. 2)
assumed.value: drawn from the same 15-stimulus population: 4 whole copies, permuted separately from the 8 test copies
assumed.reason: The paper says 60 practice trials were based on the set; their stimulus sequence is not described

assumed.item: How the positive set is announced (exp. 2)
assumed.value: shown on screen once per part, before its practice, until SPACE; then the inter-trial interval
assumed.reason: The paper says the set was announced; how is not stated

assumed.item: Wording under the announced set (exp. 2)
assumed.value: Press SPACE to start
assumed.reason: See the announcement

assumed.item: Split of the 3.7 s from response to next digit (exp. 2)
assumed.value: 0.5 s feedback light + 2.7 s inter-trial interval + 0.5 s warning
assumed.reason: Only the total is stated; the params refuse a split that does not add up to 3.7 s

assumed.item: Trials with an imperfect recall in the analysis
assumed.value: kept (a notebook switch drops them)
assumed.reason: The paper excludes wrong-lever trials (note 5) and says nothing about recall failures

assumed.item: Error criterion for rejecting a subject
assumed.value: none applied; the notebook reports each subject's error rate
assumed.reason: The paper rejected subjects who exceeded an error criterion (note 5) without stating it

assumed.item: Upper bound for a parallel process
assumed.value: Hartley-David bound on the s = 1 negative latencies: m1 + sd1 (s - 1)/sqrt(2s - 1)
assumed.reason: The paper cites the bound (notes 15-16) but its application was 'in preparation'; this is our reading

tasks.title: Experiment 1: varied-set procedure
tasks.summary: A series of 1-6 different digits, 1.2 s each; a 2.0-s delay; a warning signal; a test digit answered yes or no; a feedback light; ordered recall of the series.

parameters.name: set_sizes
parameters.label: Series lengths
parameters.meaning: The numbers of digits in a series, s (paper: p. 652).

parameters.name: item_duration
parameters.label: Digit duration
parameters.meaning: How long each digit of the series is shown (paper: p. 652).

parameters.name: item_gap
parameters.label: Gap between digits
parameters.meaning: Blank between successive digits of the series. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.label: Delay
parameters.meaning: Blank after the last digit, before the warning signal (paper: p. 652).

parameters.name: digit_height_dva
parameters.label: Text height
parameters.meaning: Font size of the digits (PsychoPy text height). ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: warning_symbol
parameters.label: Warning signal
parameters.meaning: What the warning signal is: a symbol at the digit locus. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: warning_duration
parameters.label: Warning signal duration
parameters.meaning: How long the warning is shown; the test digit appears at its offset. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: positive_key
parameters.label: Yes key
parameters.meaning: The key for 'the test digit is in memory' (the paper's positive lever). ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: negative_key
parameters.label: No key
parameters.meaning: The key for 'not in memory' (the paper's negative lever). ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: response_timeout
parameters.label: Response deadline

parameters.name: feedback_duration

parameters.name: recall_timeout

parameters.name: iti
parameters.label: Inter-trial interval

parameters.name: practice.n_per_condition
parameters.label: Practice trials per cell
parameters.meaning: Practice trials per (set size, response type) cell: 24 in all (paper: p. 652); the even split is ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: paradigm.n_per_condition
parameters.label: Test trials per cell
parameters.meaning: Test trials per (set size, response type) cell: 144 in all (paper: p. 652); the even split is inferred, ASSUMED, not in the paper.

outcomes.name: CORRECT
outcomes.meaning: The key matched the test digit: yes for a digit in memory, no for one that was not.

outcomes.name: WRONG
outcomes.meaning: The other key (the paper's 'wrong lever'); excluded from the latency analysis (note 5).

outcomes.name: NO_RESPONSE
outcomes.meaning: No key before the deadline; the condition is served again later in the block.

events.name: ITEM_ON
events.meaning: A digit of the series was shown; payload: position, digit.

events.name: PROBE_ON
events.meaning: The test digit was shown; reaction time runs from this flip.

events.name: PROBE_DIGIT
events.meaning: Same flip as PROBE_ON; payload: the digit.

events.name: FEEDBACK_ON
events.meaning: The feedback light came on; payload: correct (true/false).

events.name: RECALL_DONE
events.meaning: The recall ended; payload: what was typed, committed.

tasks.title: Experiment 2: fixed-set procedure
tasks.summary: Three parts with positive sets of 1, 2 and 4 digits, each announced once; per trial a warning signal, a test digit drawn from the paper's 15-stimulus population, a yes/no key and a feedback light; 3.7 s from a response to the next digit.

parameters.name: part_order
parameters.label: Order of the parts
parameters.meaning: Positive-set sizes in the order run; null = random per session. The paper ran s = 1, 2 and 4 (p. 652-653); the order is ASSUMED, not in the paper.
